subject: Reserved capacity commit term & pricing sensitivity — action plan and approvals
messages:
From: Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmeai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: vendor_ops@acmeai.com
Date: 2026-10-12T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP and reserved capacity ask — Acme AI

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're building a high-volume inference pipeline for our customer-facing experiences and want to explore a reserved capacity commit. Attached is our RFP and a rough monthly token/execution profile. Top-level asks: 1) a 36-month reserved commitment option (we can consider 24/36), 2) clear pass-through or indexation mechanics if GPU market costs move > +/- 15%, and 3) an initial discount schedule tied to committed GPU-hours.

Can you send sizing guidance and a pricing sensitivity view? Our procurement window is tight — we'd like a term sheet and a model by EOD next Tuesday (2026-10-19). If there are mandatory approval thresholds for deeper discounts, call those out so we can keep our internal timelines aligned.

Attached: Acme_RFP_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Jenna
Jenna Lee
Head of Procurement — Acme AI
jenna.lee@acmeai.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP and reserved capacity ask — Acme AI

Jenna — thanks, got the RFP and profile. Quick response below, will follow with an attached scenario workbook.

Key items we need to align on now:
- Baseline sizing: your profile maps to ~18k A100-equivalent GPU hours / month under our standard packing assumptions. That suggests a Reserved tier of 3 x pool units (roughly 600 GPUs) to meet 99th pct burst.
- Term tradeoffs: 12/24/36-month options. Deeper upfront discount for 36 months but higher exposure to GPU-market cost swings.
- Indexation: we propose a quarterly GPU-cost collar (band +/-12% relative to our published monthly GPU index) that adjusts per-token unit price for material moves. Alternative is an annual true-up.
- Discounts & approvals: discounts >20% off list require Finance + CRO signoff; >30% require exec (CFO) escalation.

I've attached commit_scenarios_steph_v1.xlsx with three sizing/price scenarios and a simple sensitivity on GPU cost moves. Karthik — can you run a more detailed pricing model and include an approval ladder/policy? Marissa — please flag any finance constraints or caps on cumulative exposure.

We'll aim to get the scenario workbook back by EOD Monday so Jenna has it for Tuesday's procurement review.

- Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP and reserved capacity ask — Acme AI

Attaching a sensitivity model (pricing_sensitivity_model.csv) and a short note on conditional pricing constructs. TL;DR: for the 36-month committable base (estimated 18k A100-hrs/month) we see three practical commercial constructs — pick one to iterate:

1) Fixed discount schedule: flat % off list by term (12m=12%, 24m=18%, 36m=25%). Simple, predictable for Acme, but Redwood bears market risk.
2) Indexation collar: base price with quarterly adjustment tied to GPU index; collar +/-12% with a 50/50 sharing for moves beyond collar. Lower initial discount (12m=10%, 36m=16%) but lower Redwood exposure.
3) Hybrid trigger: 36m with front-loaded discount plus an annual true-up if market GPU spot average moves >20% year-over-year — also includes a cap on cumulative rebate to protect marginal economics.

Model assumptions: list token cost mapped to GPU-hr, expected utilization (70% steady state), prefix cache savings (10%), expected uplift patterns from Acme's profile. I included a waterfall that shows Redwood's incremental gross margin under each scenario and a sensitivity column showing margin erosion per +10% GPU price move.

Approval path (recommended): discounts up to 20% can be approved by CRO+Finance manager; discounts 20–30% require CRO + CFO notification; >30% is exec escalation and needs Treasury/Head of Risk sign-off. Please note: any hybrid with deep front-loaded rebate requires a documented hedging plan or a deal-level GPU-price pass-through clause.

Next steps: Stephanie — please confirm which construct Acme prefers. Marissa — need your read on cumulative exposure (we've modeled a 36m worst-case erosion of ~9% gross margin in scenario C). Jenna — any preference on fixed vs indexed?

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP and reserved capacity ask — Acme AI

Looping in a short finance read: we ran the three constructs through our quarterly cash/ASC modeling and the practical constraints are:
- We can support up to a 25% effective discount for a 36-month term provided there's either an indexation clause (quarterly true-up) or a capped cumulative rebate.
- Anything >25% materially increases our working capital and requires a deal-level escrow / credit enhancement or an up-front partial prepayment.
- For the hybrid construct, require a maximum cumulative rebate cap at 40% of the initial discount pool and a contingency trigger to allow Redwood to transition Acme to Dedicated Shared pools if sustained GPU cost inflation exceeds 18% for two consecutive quarters.

If Acme needs a >25% effective economic they should consider a partial prepayment or a 24m front-loaded credit schedule that amortizes into the term. I'll flag this is a procurement negotiation lever.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmeai.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP and reserved capacity ask — Acme AI

Jenna — thanks for the patience. Based on the materials and the models submitted, Redwood is willing to offer the following starter commercial:

- Term: 36 months, baseline committed GPU-hours: 18k A100-equivalent hrs/month
- Pricing: 18% discount off list, with a quarterly GPU-cost indexation collar of +/-12%. For quarterly moves beyond the collar, we implement a 50/50 sharing on incremental cost changes (cap of 12% per year total).
- Protection: a cumulative rebate cap equal to 40% of the initial discount pool and an operational clause that allows temporary transition to shared Dedicated capacity if GPU-cost inflation >18% over two consecutive quarters.
- Approval: this offer is within the approved commercial bands; anything more aggressive (additional 5%+) will need CFO sign-off and a potential credit enhancement.

Please confirm acceptance of the high-level terms and we'll push a term sheet + redlines. If you want an alternative with a higher up-front discount, note it will require partial prepayment or an escrow.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
